title: Red tide-causing organism detected in Carigara Bay waters

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — Seawater samples collected from Carigara Bay tested positive for Pyrodinium bahamense, a toxic microorganism associated with paralytic shellfish poisoning, the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) said in an advisory on Tuesday. The positive samples were collected from waters covering parts of Babatngon, San Miguel, Capoocan, Barugo and Carigara, all in Leyte. The detection of Pyrodinium bahamense, a dinoflagellate commonly associated with red tide events in Philippine waters, has prompted authorities to monitor the affected areas and remind coastal communities and consumers to observe existing shellfish safety advisories.
